mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over two consecutive quarters signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -3% AND HOUST < previous year's average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from baseline during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and lowers profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals an aggressive monetary easing, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations through lower discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS falls below 1% and UNRATE exceeds 7%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in real personal income (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signals improving consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA AND RSAFS > 12-month MA for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in unemployment rate to below 5% while payroll growth accelerates signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to margin compression.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% AND PAYEMS YoY growth > 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of tight labor market and accelerated payroll growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in industrial production above its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months signals a broad-based supply expansion, which typically coincides with higher earnings and positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA for eight consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months.
